subject: Reserved pool token bandwidth addendum and renewal scope
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Alice Morgan <alice@datasolve.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved pool token bandwidth addendum and renewal scope

Alice —

Thanks again for the productive renewal call today. Per our discussion, I’m circulating a compact addendum that captures the Dedicated capacity expansion for your renewal: +4 reserved GPUs (Nvidia A100 equivalent), a dedicated reserved pool, and an explicit throughput guarantee for the pool expressed in tokens/sec.

Key summary here so we’re aligned before legal picks it up:
- Reserved capacity: +4 GPUs in your existing dedicated pool (total reserved GPUs after renewal: 12)
- Reservation window: 12-month renewal term starting on 2027-01-01
- Throughput guarantee: Reserved pool shall sustain 4,200 tokens/sec (aggregate) with a monthly availability SLO of 99.0%
- Burst allowance: auto-scaling burst up to an additional 20% for up to 10 minutes per incident (no charge for bursts within that window)
- Remedies: service credits tied to monthly SLO misses (0.5% credit per 0.25% below SLO up to 10% cap)

I attached a draft addendum (redwood-dedicated-addendum-v2.pdf) and a short SLO draft (slo-draft-token-bandwidth.txt) that shows explicit definitions for tokens, measurement windows, and exclusion events (e.g., scheduled maintenance, customer-caused networking interruptions).

Can you confirm those numbers look right from your planning side (especially the 4,200 tokens/sec target)? If yes, I’ll loop in Neha (legal) for the contractual language. If you need a different measurement basis (tokens/min or requests/sec), tell me and we’ll adapt the wording.

Next steps: confirm throughput and procurement contact, then we’ll send a DocuSign-ready addendum.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
From: Alice Morgan <alice@datasolve.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Ramirez <c.ramirez@datasolve.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 09:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Reserved pool token bandwidth addendum and renewal scope

Karthik —

Thanks for the summary and the attachments. Overall it looks close to what we discussed. A couple of clarifying items from our engineering and procurement teams:

1) Measurement unit: Our infra team prefers tokens/min for simpler quota planning. Can you confirm 4,200 tokens/sec translates to 252,000 tokens/min?
2) Burst semantics: We need to understand whether bursts are purely autoscaling on Redwood side or gated by our ingress (we occasionally see upstream spikes). If the burst is triggered by an upstream event outside your control, how does that interact with the SLO?
3) Remedies: procurement is used to service credits but also prefers a single-point SLA cap rather than tiered percentages.

I copied Carlos (procurement) so he can flag any billing/contract questions. From our side, if we can confirm the tokens/min and see a short SLO clause with explicit measurement windows, we can sign.

Appreciate it —
Alice
VP Product — DataSolve Inc.
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alice Morgan <alice@datasolve.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved pool token bandwidth addendum and renewal scope

Alice —

Quick follow-up on the two asks:

1) Units: yes, 4,200 tokens/sec = 252,000 tokens/min. We can include the tokens/min equivalent in the addendum to avoid ambiguity.

2) Burst mechanics: the burst allowance we described is an autoscaling behavior on Redwood’s side triggered by request rate to the reserved pool. If the spike is caused by upstream (your) ingress, it will still be handled by the burst path. For SLO calculations, we exclude bursts that are handled by the auto-burst window; the intent of the burst allowance is to provide a short buffer to absorb spikes without counting against the SLO.

3) Credits: we can adapt to a single-tier credit schedule if that’s preferred. Suggested language below (we’ll pass to legal):

- Monthly Throughput SLO: Reserved pool sustains 252,000 tokens/min (4,200 tokens/sec) with 99.0% availability.
- Failure Remedy: If monthly availability falls below 99.0%, DataSolve will receive a service credit equal to 5% of that month’s Dedicated capacity charges.

We’ll ask legal to craft precise definitions and exclusion clauses. If that approach works for you, we’ll prepare a DocuSign envelope next week.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference
From: Carlos Ramirez <c.ramirez@datasolve.com>

Cc: Alice Morgan <alice@datasolve.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 11:41:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Reserved pool token bandwidth addendum and renewal scope

Marissa / Karthik —

Procurement here. A few contract-side redlines we expect to submit:

• Cap on credits: we’ll accept a single-tier credit but request a cap at 25% of the monthly Dedicated capacity charges (instead of unlimited liability).
• Measurement window: need a clear UTC-based window for the measurement (e.g., calendar month UTC).
• Escalation: please include a dedicated Redwood contact for SLO investigations with a 48-hour response SLA.

We’ll run the draft addendum by our legal team but flagging these items early. Otherwise the capacity numbers look fine.

Regards,
Carlos
Head of Procurement — DataSolve Inc.
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Morgan <alice@datasolve.com>, Carlos Ramirez <c.ramirez@datasolve.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Reserved pool token bandwidth addendum and renewal scope

Team / DataSolve —

Drafting notes from Legal (high level) — please review and confirm we can include these in the addendum:

Definitions
- "Tokens" means approximate token count as measured by Redwood’s tokenization pipeline (BPE tokenization at inference ingestion). Parties agree measurement methodology is Redwood’s production tokenizer versioned in the addendum.
- "Monthly Availability" means the percentage of seconds in a UTC calendar month during which aggregate throughput of the reserved pool met or exceeded 252,000 tokens/min sustained for a rolling 5-minute window.

SLO and Remedies
- Monthly Availability SLO: 99.0%
- Remedy: If Monthly Availability < 99.0%, customer receives a credit equal to 5% of that month’s Dedicated capacity charges for every 0.5 percentage point below the SLO, capped at 25% of that month’s Dedicated capacity charges.

Exclusions
- Scheduled maintenance with >= 72 hours notice, customer network incidents, and force majeure events will be excluded from calculations.

Operational commitments
- Redwood will provide an SLO investigation contact and respond to initial investigation requests within 48 hours; a written root cause analysis will be delivered within 10 business days for any monthly SLO miss.

If DataSolve accepts the above framework, we will incorporate it into the addendum and send a DocuSign envelope.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference

Subject: Final addendum and DocuSign link — Dedicated capacity + token bandwidth SLO

Alice / Carlos —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the redlines. Per Neha’s language above (and the single-tier credit cap requested by Carlos), we’ve finalized the addendum. Main points: +4 GPUs reserved, 252,000 tokens/min reserved pool, Monthly Availability SLO 99.0%, credit schedule capped at 25% of monthly Dedicated charges.

I’ve initiated a DocuSign envelope here: https://www.docusign.com/DocuSign/link?envelopeId=abc123-ds-4371 (also linked in metadata). The envelope includes: redwood-dedicated-addendum-v2.pdf (with the SLO language) and the signature page for the renewal amendment.

Requested next steps:
- DataSolve: please have the procurement/legal team sign the DocuSign by 2026-11-12 to lock the renewal pricing and capacity start date.
- Redwood: we’ll provision the +4 GPUs into a staging reserved pool the week after signature and coordinate a go-live on 2027-01-01.

If you’d like a short call to walk through SLO measurement examples before signature, we can host 30 minutes this week — ping me preferred times.

Appreciate the collaboration — looking forward to getting this over the line.

Karthik
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
